# Part 1: Calculate a confidence interval for the proportion of green beads

What is the proportion of green beads in the bin?  In this part of your lab assignment you will build a confidence interval to answer this question.

This time, we do know the proportion, but it will not be revealed to you right away.

**TASK 1.1** If you are completing this in the classroom, go to one of the bins and take one sample.  If you are completing this lab remotely, go to the link from the lecture video page.  Report the sample size and the sample estimate for your sample, using correct notation.

To build the confidence interval, we must estimate the standard error of the statistic in 1.1.  You will do this by calculating the standard deviation of the bootstrap distribution.  

**TASK 1.2** Describe the process of drawing a bootstrap sample for this example.  Be specific.

**TASK 1.3** Once you have a bootstrap sample, what will you record from it to start generating the bootstrap distribution?

**TASK 1.4**  Modify and run the code below to generate 2000 bootstrap statistics.  Report the approximate middle of your bootstrap distribution.

    **Response**

```{r}
# reserve space for your bootstrap statistics

#modify the value of 'NumberSamples'
BootStats <- rep(NA, 2000)

# generate bootstrap samples and save statistics

# modify the values of 'NumberSamples', 'NumberWhite', 'NumberGreen', 'n'
for(i in 1:2000){
  TempSample <- sample(c(rep("White",54),rep("Green",46)), 
                       size = 100,
                       replace = T )
  
  BootStats[i] <- sum(TempSample=="Green")/100 # modify 'n'
}

# write some code here to determine the middle of your bootstrap distributing
# Determine the middle of your bootstrap distribution (median)
bootstrap_median <- median(BootStats)

# Output the median
#bootstrap_median
# Calculate the 95% confidence interval
lower_bound <- quantile(BootStats, 0.025)
upper_bound <- quantile(BootStats, 0.975)

# Output the median, standard error, and confidence interval
list(
  median = bootstrap_median,
  standard_error = standard_error,
  confidence_interval = c(lower_bound, upper_bound)
)

```

**TASK 2.6** Now generate your bootstrap distribution using at least 2000 bootstrap samples. Visualize your bootstrap distribution and describe the shape of the bootstrap distribution.

```{r}
# reserve space for your bootstrap statistics
BootStats2 <- rep(NA, 2000) # modify NumberSamples

# generate bootstrap samples and save statistics
for(i in 1:2000){ # Modify NumberSamples
  TempSample <- sample(MyResponses, 
                       size = 15, #modify n2
                       replace = T )
  BootStats2[i] <- mean(~TempSample)
}

# write some code here to visualize your bootstrap distribution
```

**TASK 2.9** Now estimate the 95% confidence interval using the formula from class (stat - 2SE, stat + 2SE).

    **Response**

```{r}
sample_mean <- mean(BootStats2)

# Assuming standard_error is previously calculated
# Calculate the 95% confidence interval using the formula
lower_bound <- sample_mean - 2 * standard_error
upper_bound <- sample_mean + 2 * standard_error

# Print the confidence interval
c(lower_bound, upper_bound)

```

# Part 3: Do people who had dogs growing up exercise more?

At the beginning of the semester your class answered questions in the class data survey.  We will now use your responses to answer the research question: "Do people who grew up with dogs exercise more?"

**TASK 3.1** What is the explanatory variable and what is the response variable?

    **Response**
    
**TASK 3.2** Which parameter are we going to make inference about?  Use correct notation.

    **Response**
    
**TASK 3.3** Load the dataset into R.  Write code to determine how many observations are there within each group (Dog - Yes/No)?  Hint: tally.

    **Response**

```{r}
ClassData <- read.csv(file.choose())
glimpse(ClassData)

# write code to determine sample size for Dog (Yes/No) groups
sample_sizes <- ClassData %>%
  group_by(Dog) %>%
  summarise(SampleSize = n())

# Print the sample sizes for each group
print(sample_sizes)

```

**TASK 3.4** Create a visualization of the data and summarize what you see here, specifically discuss what your visualization reveals about the answer to your research question.

    **Response** 
    
```{r}
gf_histogram(ExerciseMinutes ~ Dog, 
           data = ClassData, 
           fill = ~ Dog)
```


**TASK 3.5** What is your sample estimate for the population parameter?  Use correct notation, and the order can be (yes) - (no).

    **Response** 

```{r}
mean_yes <- mean(ClassData$ExerciseMinutes[ClassData$Dog == "Yes"])
mean_no <- mean(ClassData$ExerciseMinutes[ClassData$Dog == "No"])

# Calculate the difference
difference <- mean_yes - mean_no

# Print the result rounded to three decimal places
rounded_difference <- round(difference, 3)
print(rounded_difference)
```

**TASK 3.6** Modify the code below to generate a bootstrap distribution using at least 2000 samples. 

    **Response**

```{r}
# reserve space for your bootstrap statistics
BootStats3 <- rep(NA, 2000) # modify NumberSamples

# generate bootstrap samples and save statistics
for(i in 1:2000){ # modify NumberSamples
  TempSample <- rbind(sample_n(ClassData  |> filter(Dog =="Yes"), 
                       size = 102,  # modify n_yes to be sample size for Dog Yes
                       replace = T ),
                      sample_n(ClassData  |> filter(Dog =="No"), 
                       size = 22,  # modify n_no to be sample size for Dog No
                       replace = T )
  )

  BootStats3[i] <- diff(mean(ExerciseMinutes ~ Dog, data = TempSample))
}

# write some code here to visualize your bootstrap distribution
gf_histogram(~BootStats3, data = data.frame(BootStats3))

```

**TASK 3.7** Use the code chunk below to calculate and report the standard error of the difference in sample means.  Remember that the standard error is the standard deviation of a statistic.

    **Response**
    
```{r}
standard_error <- sd(BootStats3)

# Print the standard error rounded to three decimal places
#rounded_standard_error <- round(standard_error, 3)
print(standard_error)
```


**TASK 3.8**	Using percentiles, find a 95% confidence interval for the difference of population means.

    **Response**
    
```{r}
#c(quantile(BootStats3,quantile(BootStats3, 0.025)), quantile(BootStats3,quantile(BootStats3, 0.975)))  # modify 'LowerProp' and 'UpperProp'

lower_bound <- quantile(BootStats3, 0.025)
upper_bound <- quantile(BootStats3, 0.975)
confidence_interval <- c(lower_bound, upper_bound)
print(confidence_interval)
```

**TASK 3.9** Find a 98% confidence interval for the difference of population means.

```{r}
upper_bound_98 <- quantile(BootStats3, 0.99)

# Print the confidence interval rounded to three decimal places

#rounded_confidence_interval_98 <- round(confidence_interval_98, 3)
```
